attribution_limitations: "No significant surgical history" is stated in the same paragraph as a 2015 four-vessel CABG; the qualifier "significant" may mean relevant to the hernia, but the source does not say so.

limitations: No figures or supplements are listed in the source.
The discussion hypothesizes that postoperative hematomas evolved into hydroceles by compressing lymphatic vessels; this is speculation and is not recorded as a patient fact.
The 59-year-old patient in the discussion belongs to a cited 2023 case report and is not an index patient.
The two TAPP operations were performed within a 5-week interval at the same facility; the interval is between the two patients and is not assigned to either one.
Patient 1 hydrocele is named only in the abstract and the introduction sentence; the case narrative describes the left scrotal fluid collection on ultrasound without the word hydrocele.

Abstract says symptoms gradually resolved without surgery, while the case text keeps pain on direct contact (patient 1) and mild tenderness on palpation (patient 2); both are recorded as written, not reconciled.
Patient 2 is said to have no significant surgical history despite a documented 2015 CABG; the absent surgical-history item is kept review_only (ambiguous qualifier).
Anchors for relative times such as "3 years earlier" and "1 month later" are not stated and are left null.

Parent review: the abstract statement that symptoms gradually resolved without surgery is undated and is judged compatible with (not contradicted by) the case text, which reports improvement with residual contact pain (patient 1) or mild tenderness (patient 2) at the last dated visit; both views are recorded.

limitations: No figures or supplements are listed in the source.
The discussion hypothesizes that postoperative hematomas evolved into hydroceles by compressing lymphatic vessels; this is speculation and is not recorded as a patient fact.
The 59-year-old patient in the discussion belongs to a cited 2023 case report and is not an index patient.
The two TAPP operations were performed within a 5-week interval at the same facility; the interval is between the two patients and is not assigned to either one.
Patient 1 hydrocele is named only in the abstract and the introduction sentence; the case narrative describes the left scrotal fluid collection on ultrasound without the word hydrocele.

Abstract says symptoms gradually resolved without surgery, while the case text keeps pain on direct contact (patient 1) and mild tenderness on palpation (patient 2); both are recorded as written, not reconciled.
Patient 2 is said to have no significant surgical history despite a documented 2015 CABG; the absent surgical-history item is kept review_only (ambiguous qualifier).
Anchors for relative times such as "3 years earlier" and "1 month later" are not stated and are left null.

Parent review: the abstract statement that symptoms gradually resolved without surgery is undated and is judged compatible with (not contradicted by) the case text, which reports improvement with residual contact pain (patient 1) or mild tenderness (patient 2) at the last dated visit; both views are recorded.
